topic_summary: Analysis of end-of-life decision-making frameworks where the shared commitment to 'dignified death' is read through competing interpretive lenses: autonomy-primary (self-determination as paramount) versus sanctity-of-life-primary (life preservation as paramount). Each reading generates structurally distinct constraints with different victim sets and authority structures.

key_entities: Terminally ill patient (rights-holder under autonomy reading; protected life under sanctity reading)
Medical practitioner (agent of patient will vs guardian of life)
State regulatory apparatus (licensing, criminal law enforcement)
Religious/philosophical authority structures (natural law, divine command, secular humanism)
key_tensions: Individual self-determination vs collective duty to protect life
Suffering relief vs slippery slope to coerced death

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The shared commitment that 'death should occur with dignity' — a stabilized norm all parties invoke but read through incompatible interpretive frameworks
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Autonomy reading: individual as sole legitimate interpreter of own dignity. Sanctity reading: transcendent moral law (religious or natural law) as interpretive authority, with state/medical profession as enforcement agents

readings.commitment: Dignity resides in self-determination; suffering individual has final authority over timing and method of death
readings.authority_grounding: Liberal autonomy doctrine; Millian harm principle; patient sovereignty in medical ethics
readings.expected_structural_delta: Victim set: those denied exit (suffering prolonged against will). Beneficiary: autonomous agent. High ε for state prohibition (0.45-0.60 range). Constraint type: tangled_rope (autonomy norm entangled with medical gatekeeping, eligibility criteria).

readings.commitment: Dignity resides in life's intrinsic value; intentional life-termination violates transcendent moral law regardless of consent
readings.authority_grounding: Natural law tradition; religious doctrine (Catholic, Islamic, Orthodox Jewish); vitalist medical ethics
readings.expected_structural_delta: Victim set: vulnerable populations subject to coercion/pressure (elderly, disabled, poor). Beneficiary: moral order / community. High ε for legalization (0.50-0.65 range). Constraint type: snare (protection norm becomes coercive prolongation of suffering).

readings.commitment: Dignity emerges from relational context; decision authority distributed across patient-family-clinician triad with procedural safeguards
readings.authority_grounding: Feminist care ethics; communitarian bioethics; Belgian/Dutch regulatory models
readings.expected_structural_delta: Victim set: those excluded from decision-making process (patient in pure autonomy model, vulnerable in pure sanctity model). Beneficiary: relational network. Moderate ε (0.30-0.45 range). Constraint type: rope (coordination problem with high procedural overhead).

axes.structural_delta: Individual sovereignty over own death; state prohibition as rights violation
axes.primary_observable: Legal permissibility of physician-assisted death; patient eligibility criteria breadth
axes.selection_reason: Core reading with distinct victim set and high structural tension with sibling readings

axes.structural_delta: Life's intrinsic value transcends individual preference; legalization as moral hazard
axes.primary_observable: Criminal prohibition scope; conscientious objection protections for medical practitioners
axes.selection_reason: Structurally opposed reading with non-overlapping victim set; captures slippery slope mechanism

axes.structural_delta: Decision-making as shared process; procedural safeguards over absolute rights or prohibitions
axes.primary_observable: Regulatory framework complexity; multi-party consent requirements; waiting periods
axes.selection_reason: Third structural position attempting synthesis; captures real-world regulatory compromise models

axes.structural_delta: Physician discretion as constraint on patient autonomy; professional liability as enforcement mechanism
axes.primary_observable: Physician participation rates in jurisdictions with legal assisted death; conscientious objection prevalence
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: implementation detail downstream of autonomy_primary reading; captured in that constraint's gatekeeping dimension

axes.structural_delta: Healthcare cost burden as coercive force toward assisted death; means-testing as vulnerability amplifier
axes.primary_observable: Correlation between assisted death uptake and healthcare cost burden; insurance coverage disparities
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: specific mechanism within sanctity_primary's victim set; omega material on structural coercion

deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Implementation detail captured within autonomy_primary reading's constraint structure

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Healthcare cost as coercive force toward death
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Specific mechanism within sanctity_primary's victim set; warrants omega on structural coercion dynamics

omegas.description: Disability rights advocates argue both readings erase disabled experience: autonomy reading assumes suffering is objective; sanctity reading denies disabled agency. Is there a fourth reading grounded in disability justice that neither selected reading captures?

Does economic pressure (deferred axis economic_coercion) constitute a distinct constraint or amplify sanctity_primary's victim set? If healthcare cost burden systematically channels vulnerable populations toward assisted death, the rope of relational_autonomy becomes a snare.
omegas.source: Deferred axis economic_coercion + Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan)

omegas.description: Do non-Western frameworks (e.g., Confucian filial piety, Ubuntu communalism) constitute additional readings or cultural implementations of relational_autonomy? Extraction limited by Western bioethics training data.
omegas.source: F34 (Epistemic Trespass) + Dark Matter Probe 1 (Operational Medium)

omegas.description: Are these readings stable across jurisdictions or do they drift under implementation pressure? Oregon's Death with Dignity Act (autonomy-primary in statute) shows procedural accretion toward relational model in practice.

fracture_scan.notes: F34 detected: Analysis grounded in Western bioethics literature (Beauchamp/Childress, Dworkin, Callahan). Non-Western frameworks (Confucian, Ubuntu, Islamic bioethics) may constitute distinct readings not captured. Generated omega_cultural_variation to bound this limitation. Relational_autonomy reading draws on feminist care ethics but may inadequately represent non-Western communitarian traditions.
